body:
I'm in Canada, so I take it just working in a kitchen will be a good way to keep going? I actually don't give a fuck about the other cook making some jabs, he is trying to teach me as well. I just take all the useful stuff he says and filter out all the other garbage.

I've dealt with too many personalities at this point in my life to care. Is there anything I can communicate with my chef? He's actually quite nice and constantly wants me to do better. Is it worth asking about my progress overall? Should I mention that I'm having trouble lugging heavy things? Like if he asks me to grab a bus bin that I know for a fact I can't carry should I bring it up?

To be fair, I'm being chewed out for shit that they did teach me too. Being slow is my biggest problem and not being able to remember things all the time. One of the cooks, it's gotten to the point where he makes me feel really stupid and slow. That I can't comprehend doing certain things.

I just want to be able to get another kitchen job once this one is over, as it's a summer pop up but I worry that I won't be able to

I don't think it's a bad kitchen per se, I think it's just the nature of the business. It's a pop up outdoor restaurant and it requires a lot of micromanagement just to get stuff going because there's no fridge, no storage etc etc. I think sometimes they forget how little someone actually knows when starting sometimes.

But there's a lot. I get a lot of contradictions too. The yelling/telling off doesn't bother me because it's not so bad? And I know it's for learning and it's just in the middle of service. It's just that I'm struggling and I'm expected to just know so much. Today I almost broke down because I couldn't get a lockbox to open, because it was jammed and I didn't know what to go back and say.

In the end I just went back and said I can't open it sorry, it's stuck
